_readme: Reference classes the decision card shows next to every model probability (outside view first: insight:lit-base-rate-neglect-outside-view). Each class says where it came from and how it is biased. null = no honest number on file; the card prints 'n/a' rather than inventing one. v2 (2026-11-23): two survivorship-free 5-year classes computed from the stage-2 back-test panels (method: research_notes/Backtests/base_rates_5y.md). Old classes are kept with a _deprecated suffix; the card resolves an old name to its _deprecated entry and says so. ci95 = 95% bootstrap interval; bounds = range under the alternative missing-data assumption; size_band lets the card warn when a company sits outside the class. v3 (2026-11-25): India lender class india_lender_1000_20000cr_5y (research_notes/Backtests/base_rates_lenders_india.md); decision_card v1.5 picks it automatically for a firm marked as a lender. No US lender class yet or for India mcap > Rs 20,000 cr / US float > $10B.

india_lender_1000_20000cr_5y.label: India lenders (banks, SFBs, NBFCs, HFCs, financial institutions), mcap Rs 1,000-20,000 cr at T, 5 yrs from 30-Sep-2016 and 30-Sep-2018 (census of lender candidates incl. merged, delisted and failed lenders; equal weight)
india_lender_1000_20000cr_5y.caveats: Two start dates only and they disagree sharply (2016 start: P(>=3x) 4%, P(<=0.5x) 42%, blow-up 35% - PSU-bank NPA cycle, IL&FS/DHFL credit freeze and the Mar-2020 crash all inside the window; 2018 start: 18% / 9% / 20%); CIs show sampling error only. Blow-up uses the price rule (close <=0.2x the T close at any point), so the Mar-2020 COVID crash counts even where the stock later recovered: the permanent share (blow-up AND R5 <=0.5x or no R5) is 19.6%. Price only (dividends excluded, ~1-2%/yr). Frame = lender-keyword names on BSE/NSE active, delisted and suspended lists + industry map + explicit cases; lenders with no keyword in their name that have since died are missed. Mergers chained into the acquirer at the target's last price (PSU-bank amalgamations, GRUH, Capital First, Bharat Financial, SBI associates, Shriram City, Equitas). Syndicate Bank excluded (broken price series); YES Bank and Indiabulls Housing were above Rs 20,000 cr at both T so their episodes are NOT in the class; IL&FS group had no listed lender; PMC Bank was not listed. 4 size overrides (RBL 2016, CreditAccess 2018 IPO-month; single-source).

india_nonfin_1000_20000cr_5y.label: India non-financial, mcap Rs 1,000-20,000 cr at T, 5 yrs from 30-Sep-2016 and 30-Sep-2018 (survivorship-free, dead firms included, stratum-weighted)
india_nonfin_1000_20000cr_5y.caveats: n=208 company-snapshots (54 distress-census D, 153 live L at weight 5.63, 1 delisted-other X at 4.26); 95% CIs (company bootstrap within stratum): P(>=3x) 14.1-28.7%, P(<=0.5x) 7.0-16.1%, P(blow-up) 10.2-21.4%. Two start dates only, and they disagree (2016: >=3x 16%, blow-up 21%; 2018: 26%, 10%). Price return only (no dividends, ~1%/yr). Blow-up = close <=0.2x the close at T, liquidation or compulsory delisting (no fraud field). Remaining survivorship leak toward FEWER failures (IBBI firms renamed/merged and 221 IBBI rows without identifiers missing; voluntary/merger delistings X under-covered). A survivors-only sample from the same frame says P(<=0.5x) 7% instead of 11%.

us_float_500m_10b_5y.label: US non-financial, non-utility 10-K filers, public float $500M-$10B at T, 5 yrs from 30-Jun-2015/2017/2019 (survivorship-free: EDGAR fates for unpriced firms)
us_float_500m_10b_5y.caveats: n=3125 firm-snapshots used of 3,691 in band (1,823 firms; 2,074 priced, 152 unpriced EDGAR failures, 899 unpriced acquisitions counted as neither tail; 566 unpriced alive/stopped-filing/exchange-transfer rows excluded as missing at random). 95% CIs (CIK bootstrap): P(>=3x) 6.0-8.1%, P(<=0.5x) 12.7-15.7%, P(blow-up) 9.6-12.3%. Assumption bounds (acquisitions excluded instead of neutral): P(>=3x) up to 9.8%, P(<=0.5x) up to 19.9%, blow-up up to 15.3%. Three start dates (2015: >=3x 5.4%, <=0.5x 17.3%; 2017: 5.9%, 9.9%; 2019: 9.5%, 14.9%); windows include the 2015-16 energy bust, COVID and 2022. Total return (adjusted close). Float is stale and understates controlled firms' market cap. Blow-up excludes fraud findings and misses firms that fell 80% and were then bought (unpriced).

india_survivors_2020_25_mcap_ge400_depre.label: India, random NSE sample, mcap >= Rs 400 cr at T0, 5 yrs from 30-Sep-2020
india_survivors_2020_25_mcap_ge400_depre.caveats: Survivors only (firms delisted before mid-2023 absent -> loss rates understated); T0 was six months after the Mar-2020 low and 2020-25 was a strong small/mid-cap bull market (-> x3 overstated). One snapshot. Treat as an upper bound for P(>=3x) and a lower bound for P(<=0.5x).
india_survivors_2020_25_mcap_ge400_depre.deprecated: 2026-11-23: superseded by india_nonfin_1000_20000cr_5y / us_float_500m_10b_5y (survivorship-free, multi-start). Kept so old cards re-run unchanged; do not use for new cards.

india_survivors_2020_25_all_deprecated.label: India, random NSE sample (all sizes), 5 yrs from 30-Sep-2020
india_survivors_2020_25_all_deprecated.caveats: Same biases as the mcap >= 400 cr class, stronger for small caps (mcap < 400 cr: x3 72%).
india_survivors_2020_25_all_deprecated.deprecated: 2026-11-23: superseded by india_nonfin_1000_20000cr_5y / us_float_500m_10b_5y (survivorship-free, multi-start). Kept so old cards re-run unchanged; do not use for new cards.

india_survivors_2020_to_nov26_all_deprec.label: India, random NSE sample, 30-Sep-2020 -> 18-Nov-2026 (~6.1 yrs)
india_survivors_2020_to_nov26_all_deprec.caveats: Includes the 2024-26 small-cap drawdown, so the loss tail is a little fatter than the 5-yr window. Survivors only.

us_ipo_3y_ritter_deprecated.label: US operating-company IPOs 1975-2021, 3-yr buy-and-hold from first close (Ritter Table 16e)
us_ipo_3y_ritter_deprecated.caveats: IPOs, not seasoned stocks, and 3 years not 5. p_ge_3x = share with BHR > +200% (6.0% + 1.3% + 0.5%). With LTM sales >= $100m the >50% loss share falls to 25.9%. Use only as a rough US left-tail anchor until a seasoned-stock 5-yr distribution is computed.

us_seasoned_5y_deprecated.source: NOT ON FILE. Needed: CRSP-style 5-yr distribution incl. delistings (stage 1). Bessembinder context only: ~58% of US stocks lose to T-bills over their lifetime (insight:bessembinder).

blowup_definition: Close falls >= 80% below the entry price at any point within the horizon, OR delisting/insolvency/suspension, OR a regulator or auditor finding of fraud or misstatement. No class above can measure this yet (survivor samples).
